name: search_investigations
description: List the 24 PSI combustion investigations as cards; filter by fire-safety pillar, fuel phase or flight/ground, and rank by a keyword query.

name: get_investigation
description: Full knowledge record of one investigation: question, physics (with equations), method, test matrix, measurements, PSI data, findings with quoted sources, fire-safety relevance, limitations, open questions; `publications` (the record's papers in order, each with a `review`: access, read_url, classification, summary, quoted items; an AI reading of the paper, null when not reviewed) and `publication_review` (counts by access and classification).

name: filter_tests
description: Rows of the per-test table (2,177 rows, of which 2,059 are single tests: fuel, O2, pressure, flow, outcomes). Use for any question about what was tested and what happened.

fuel.description: a normalised fuel name, matched as a whole word: pmma, heptane (also n-heptane blends); ethane does not return methane

config.description: substring: normal, inverse, coflow, droplet, opposed flow, concurrent flow

pressure_kpa.description: [min, max]; null leaves that end open

flow_cm_s.description: [min, max]; null leaves that end open

outcome.description: solid-fuel runs of BASS (PSI-26) and BASS-II (PSI-25) only: how the flame ended, read from the crew's notes; each row quotes its source in outcome_quote and gives outcome_cause (blowoff, low_flow, nitrogen, unspecified) when extinguished. Null on most rows: not stated

outcome_action.description: extinguished runs of BASS and BASS-II: what was done to the flow when the flame went out. flow_reduced = it went out at a finite low setting (a quenching limit, the setting in outcome_setting when stated); flow_shut_off = the crew stopped the flow to end the run (not a limit); flow_raised = blowoff; none = it went out by itself at constant flow. Null when the words do not say. flow_cm_s on these rows is the log's single air-display value, not the flow at extinction

sheet_out.description: ACME gas flames (PSI-10 inverse flames of 2021-22, PSI-159) only: the ending ticked on the test's hand-filled sheet. ext_detect = the flame went out by itself; time_out = it lasted the scripted time; temp_limit = it was cut off because the burner got too hot (neither an extinction nor a full-length flame). An AI reading of a scan, not checked by a human

exclude_flags.description: drop rows carrying any of these flag codes

sheets.description: attach to each PSI-10 / PSI-159 row its hand-filled ACME test sheet as `test_sheet`: ignited, hot or cool flame, how the flame ended (`out`), operator comments, file and page. An AI reading of a scan, not checked by a human: repeat that note

name: compare
description: Side-by-side comparison of investigations: question, fuels, tested ranges, sensors, key findings, limitations.

name: coverage
description: Count tests on a 2-D grid (default ambient O2 against pressure) and report which reference atmospheres (ISS cabin, Moon habitat, exploration, spacesuit) have no data. Use for gap questions. A reference's `nearest_test` lists in `not_measured` the columns filled from the investigation's stated range, not measured for that test.

name: relevance
description: Rank investigations by relevance to a fire-safety scenario and state how far the nearest real test is from it. fuel_phase weights the ranking and does not filter it: check `phase_match` on each row; `nearest_test` is always a test of that phase (null if none), and `closest_same_phase_test` is the nearest one overall. Never present `nearest_test_other_phase` as a test of the requested material. A condition a test dict lists in `not_measured` was not recorded for that test: a value shown for it is the middle of the investigation's range in `condition_ranges` (stated range or assumed cabin air), so say so when quoting it. Scenario names: iss-cabin, moon-habitat, mars-habitat, pressurised-rover, spacecraft-transit.

scenario.description: scenario name, or {x_o2, pressure_kpa, flow_cm_s, gravity_g}

name: find_evidence
description: Keyword search for passages: reviewed digest findings (with citation ids) and raw text of PSI documents (file and page; `transcribed` marks an AI model's reading of a scanned page). Keyword-based: use the documents' own terms and try synonyms.

name: timeseries
description: Sensor time series of one test (decimated) with summary features (burn duration, peak temperatures, chamber pressure). Available for PSI-10, PSI-23, PSI-39, PSI-159 and Saffire-I/III (PSI-98, PSI-100). For 24 PSI-39 droplet tests the investigators' reduced data (droplet diameter, hot- and cool-flame diameter, radiometer power against time) are a second recording: test_point "FLEX-<test id>-reduced". Reads the raw NASA files: from disk in a local copy; the demo server fetches each from NASA PSI on first use and caches it, so a recording nobody opened before fails with 502 while PSI is down.

name: predict
description: Small per-investigation statistical model. Without model_id: list models, their inputs, accuracy and valid domain. With model_id plus every input of that model as extra named arguments: prediction (none outside the fitted domain) and the nearest real tests. For a quantity: prediction and interval [low, high] in `unit`, interval_nominal (0.9, the target), interval_coverage (n_inside of n on held-out test days, per fuel under by.levels), interval_clipped and interval_low_unclipped (lower end cut at 0), interval_unclipped, interval_unavailable (why interval is null), prediction_below_floor (the estimate itself is below 0, so prediction and interval are null), prediction_unavailable (why prediction is null), prediction_raw (the estimate as computed, a diagnostic only), interval_method, accession (source). The full list is about 75 kB: pass compact=true to get only id, inputs with their valid domain, accuracy and what each model must not be used for.

compact.description: with no model_id: the short list (about 5 kB)

name: discrepancies
description: Errors and doubts in the original PSI experiment tables: conflicts with the raw sensor data (table value, raw value, evidence, action taken), every value this dataset changed, flag meanings and counts, statements resting on files PSI lists as removed, and `source_disagreements`: a published paper by the investigators disagreeing with the PSI data (paper quote, read_url, locator, claim), shown but never applied to the tables; say it is the paper against PSI. Use whenever the user asks about data quality or when showing a test whose row has flags.

name: document_text
description: Our extracted text of one PSI file, so a scanned PDF without a text layer can be read and copied. Without page: the pages (locators: p1, p2 for PDFs; sheet, slide or all for other files) that have text. With page: that page's passages in order (text, locator, transcribed). transcribed=true is an AI model's reading of a scan; check it in the original. A file with no text returns no pages. Use when a user reads a document, or to quote a page that find_evidence pointed to.

file.description: file name as listed in sources or the PSI catalogue
